text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- According to sources in Washington Iran planned to assassinate British writer Salman Rushdie during his visit to Copenhagen in mid-November to collect an EU literature prize. According to the newspaper the CIA tipped off the Danish government, leading to Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen's much criticised refusal "on security grounds" to allow Rushdie to come to Denmark. After a government backdown, Rushdie came to Copenhagen on November 13 to collect his prize but the affair sparked a major domestic political crisis.
--- Denmark's trade with Hong Kong is still on the increase and top Danish businessmen expect even better results in 1997 despite the impending return of the British crown colony to Chinese rule.

--- Denmark's opt-out on Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), due to be introduced in some EU member states in 1999, will be of little importance to Danish export companies, company executives say. But they say the Danish crown may become less important as a trading currency and more loans will have to be raised abroad.

--- Danish police will have to increase the number of customs officers at Copenhagen International Airport eightfold when Denmark adheres to the Schengen agreement, abolishing customs control with some other EU member states. The extra police will be needed to check passengers entering Denmark from non- Schengen nations.
--- Danish Economy Minister Marianne Jelved foresees the need for a referendum on Denmark's participation in EMU (Europe's Economic and Monetary Union) in the year 2002.
